\section[gründlich]{gründlich — thorough}

\label{lesson:GE-C216-gruendlich}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for generous, then the German for good value.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: gründlich}
\textbf{gründlich} — \textquotedblleft{}thorough\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{gründlich} is \emph{Grund}, \textquotedblleft{}ground, bottom\textquotedblright{}, + \emph{-lich}: going down to the bottom. \emph{Grund} is the same word as English \emph{ground}. (EtymDB 2.1)
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

\section[häufig]{häufig — frequent}

\label{lesson:GE-C216-haeufig}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for good value, then the German for thorough.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: häufig}
\textbf{häufig} — \textquotedblleft{}frequent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{häufig} is the word for \textquotedblleft{}a heap\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-ig}: coming in heaps, so frequent. The heap word is a cousin of English \emph{heap}.
\end{cousinweb}

\textbf{herrlich} — \textquotedblleft{}wonderful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{herrlich} $\leftarrow$ Middle High German \emph{hērlich} $\leftarrow$ Old High German \emph{hērlīh}, \textquotedblleft{}noble, splendid\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1), from \emph{hēr}, \textquotedblleft{}venerable\textquotedblright{}, first \textquotedblleft{}grey-haired\textquotedblright{}. English \emph{hoar} is a cousin.
\end{cousinweb}
